Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc-Lko:30098
Court No. - 6
Case :- Writ - A No. - 21851 of 2019
Petitioner :- Ram Lal
Respondent :- State Of U.P. Thru Prin.Secy. Home Lucknow And Ors.

Counsel for Petitioner :- Mohd. Shujauddin Waris,Sheshnath Bhardwaj Advoc
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Abdul Moin,J.
1.

Heard.
2.

The instant writ petition has been filed praying for the following main relief(s):
"(i) issue or pass a writ, direction and/or order in the nature of certiorari quashing the impugned order dated 09.07.2019 passed by the Superintendent of Police,
Railways, Lucknow as contained in Annexure No. 1 hereto, together with the report of the Screening Committee on the basis of the which the impugned order dated 09.07.2019 passed by the Superintendent of Police, Railways, Lucknow as contained in Annexure No.1 hereto was passed after summoning the originals thereof from the concerned respondents.

(ii) issue or pass a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents hereto to retain the petitioner on the post of Follower till his retirement Ram Lal vs State Of U.P. Thru Prin.Secy. Home ... on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156284268/
1 from service on attaining the age of superannuation of sixty years and pay him the salary and allowances of the said post as and when the same falls due every month."

entities.text: Ram Lal vs State Of U.P. Thru Prin.Secy. Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. The case set forth by learned counsel for the petitioner is that the petitioner had been appointed on a class IV post of Cook / Follower on 01.06.1991 and had been working since then when he has been retired compulsorily vide order dated 09.07.2019, a copy of which is annexure 1 to the petition.

4. The contention of learned counsel for the petitioner is that the respondents while filing the counter affidavit have categorically stated in paragraph 8 of the counter affidavit that a total of 53 employees including the petitioner were considered for the purpose of compulsory retirement by the Screening Committee.
Two employees, namely the petitioner as well as one Shri Ram Sumer, have been recommended for being compulsorily retired.
In pursuance thereof the petitioner has been compulsorily retired vide the order dated 09.07.2019 and Shri Ram Sumer had been compulsorily retired vide the order of same date i.e. 09.07.2019.
Shri Ram Sumer had challenged his order by filing Writ Petition No. 28975 (SS) of 2019 in re: Ram Sumer vs State of U.P. and others.

entities.text: Ram Sumer vs State of U.P. and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court vide the judgement and order dated 06.10.2021 has quashed the order of compulsorily retirement of Shri Ram Sumer and has directed for his reinstatement with all consequential benefits.
He further contends that now it is only the petitioner out of 53 employees who has been given compulsory retirement and who remains out of employment.

5. The further contention of learned counsel for the petitioner is that a perusal of counter affidavit would indicate that the respondents have considered following punishments of the petitioner during his service namely:
(a) a suspension order dated 12.06.2008,
(b) an order dated 12.06.2008 for not making payment of the period of absence as well as non payment of subsistence allowance,
(c) penalty order dated 12.08.2008,
(d) a termination from service order dated 20.01.2011,
(e) an order reverting the petitioner at minimum of pay scale vide the order dated 26.09.2018.
6.

It has further been stated in paragraph 9 of the counter affidavit that the petitioner is habitual of disobedience, remains absent from duty without permission, slackness in duty work and conduct and behavior not being satisfactory, indisciplined and not being efficient.

7. The contention is that a perusal of the chart as annexed as annexure CA-2 to the counter affidavit would indicate that the respondents have considered 10 years of confidential entries of the petitioner starting from the year 2009 and the order of compulsory retirement has been passed in the year 2019 yet the respondents have also considered the suspension order dated 12.06.2008, the Ram Lal vs State Of U.P. Thru Prin.Secy. Home ... on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156284268/
2 order dated 12.08.2008 per which he has not been given the payment for the period of his absence as well as the penalty order dated 12.08.2008 which would be contradictory to the own stand taken by the respondents in the counter affidavit of having only considered 10 years of service record in as much as the service record could only have been considered with effect from the year 2009 and not earlier and as such the aforesaid three alleged punishment orders of the year 2008 would have no relevance.
8. So far as termination order dated 20.01.2011 is concerned, it is contended that upon a challenge being raised by the petitioner to the said order by filing Writ Petition No. 725 (SS) of 2011 the writ court vide judgement and order dated 14.03.2013 had set aside the said order and had directed for reinstatement of the petitioner in service and in pursuance thereof the petitioner had already been reinstated in service and consequently there was no occasion for the respondents to have considered the termination order of the petitioner of the year 2011 which already stand set aside by writ court.
9.

entities.text: Ram Lal vs State Of U.P. Thru Prin.Secy. Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
So far as reversion in minimum pay scale by the order dated 26.09.2018 is concerned, it is contended that against the said order the petitioner had preferred an appeal and the appeal was still pending for consideration before the appellate authority at the time of passing of the order of compulsory retirement dated 09.07.2019 and once the said punishment order has not attained finality consequently there was no occasion for consideration of the said order also.
10.

So far as service records for the years 2009 to 2018 is concerned it is contended that perusal of the chart would indicate that invariably, service record of the petitioner has been satisfactory but for two years i.e. for 2011 and 2012, no entry has been indicated against the petitioner but at the same time it has also not been indicated that the service record / confidential entry of the petitioner is unsatisfactory and thus non recording of service record entry of years 2011 and 2012 cannot be read against the petitioner.
11.

Learned counsel for the petitioner also contends that in the chart which has been filed by the respondents, it has been indicated that an FIR has been lodged against the petitioner which was registered as Case Crime No. 685 of 2009 under Sections 109, 143, 188, 353, 419, 420 & 504 IPC and Section 3 of the Police (Incitement to Disaffection) Act, 1922.

In this regard it is stated that the petitioner alongwith others had formed a registered association, as would be apparent from perusal of the annexure 2 to the writ petition, as the petitioner alongwith other associates had not received the special pay which was admissible for working on Saturdays and Sundays and were protesting against the same which resulted in the FIR being lodged against him.

12. It is also contended that the association had been formed by various persons including the petitioner as would be apparent from a perusal of annexure 2 to the petition but it is only the petitioner who has been singled out for compulsory retirement which would clearly be discriminatory.

13. It is also contended that a perusal of said entries would indicate that at no stretch of time have the respondents withheld the integrity of the petitioner and consequently it cannot be said that the petitioner was having an adverse service record so as to entail the petitioner being compulsorily Ram Lal vs State Of U.P. Thru Prin.Secy. Home ... on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156284268/
3 retired from service.

entities.text: Ram Lal vs State Of U.P. Thru Prin.Secy. Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. Learned counsel for the petitioner has also stressed that the petitioner does not hold any managerial post and for that matter he is not required to supervise any staff, he being a class IV staff and always follows orders which are issued by his immediate superiors and there is nothing adverse on record which has been considered by the respondents and / or annexed to the counter affidavit to indicate either any dereliction of duty on his part or any insubordination and thus the order of compulsory retirement reflects patent non-application of mind more particularity when out of 53 employees considered for compulsory retirement, it is only the petitioner who stands out of service on account of compulsory retirement.

15. On the other hand, learned Standing Counsel appearing for the respondents has supported the order of compulsory retirement of the petitioner on the ground that the screening committee had considered the service record of the petitioner and on account of the details as mentioned in paragraphs 8 and 9 of the counter affidavit, the screening committee was of the view that the petitioner should be compulsorily retired, consequently he has been retired from service and as such there is no illegality and infirmity in the order impugned.

16. Heard learned counsels for the parties and perused the record.
17.
From perusal of record it emerge that the petitioner had been appointed on a class IV post in the year 1996.
He has been compulsorily retired vide the order dated 09.07.2019.

The reason for compulsory retirement as indicated in detail in paragraphs 8 and 9 of the counter affidavit are (a) a suspension order dated 12.06.2008, (b) an order dated 12.06.2008 for not making payment of the period of absence as well as non payment of subsistence allowance, (c) penalty order dated 12.08.2008, (d) a termination from service order dated 20.01.2011, (e) an order reverting the petitioner at minimum of pay scale vide the order dated 26.09.2018 as well as adverse service records.
18.
From perusal of the chart as annexed by the respondents as annexure CA-2 to the counter affidavit, it emerges that the respondents have considered service records for the period from 2009 to 2018.

Three of alleged punishments which have been taken into consideration by the respondents as detailed in paragraph 8 of the counter affidavit pertain to the year 2008 and thus consideration of said "punishment orders" or adverse orders of the year 2008 would be contrary to consideration of service records which the respondents profess to have considered as per chart i.e. on one hand it is stated that service records for years 2009 to 2018 have been considered while considering the case of the petitioner for compulsory retirement and on the other hand they have considered the alleged punishment orders or adverse order of the year 2008 which cannot be said to be countenanced in the eyes of law.

19. So far as punishment order dated 26.08.2019 is concerned an appeal against the said order was pending for consideration before the appellate authority and thus the said punishment was still to attain finality in as much as the appeal has been decided vide the order dated 26.08.2019, a copy of which is annexure RA-4 to the rejoinder affidavit, meaning thereby that at the time of consideration Ram Lal vs State Of U.P. Thru Prin.Secy. Home ... on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156284268/
4 of the said punishment, the order had still to attain finality.

entities.text: Ram Lal vs State Of U.P. Thru Prin.Secy. Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Elaborating the same this aspect of the matter can also be understood that in case the appeal filed by the petitioner was allowed the same would have entailed there being no punishment order against the petitioner meaning thereby that the said material would not have been adverse to the petitioner, thus there is no question of consideration of the said punishment order.
Further, the service records for the years 2009 to 2018 also indicate that invariably, the petitioner is having a satisfactory service record.

For two years i.e.
2011 and 2012 no entry has been indicated but it is not the case of the respondents that the petitioner has either been graded as unsatisfactory or poor.
It is also not the case of the respondents that at any stretch of time the petitioners' integrity has been withheld.

What the respondents have lost sight of while passing the order of compulsory retirement is that the petitioner was working on a class IV post and is not working either in a managerial capacity or in a supervisory capacity.

Certain facts as indicated in paragraph 9 of the counter affidavit of the petitioner being a habitual absentee or not following the orders of superior authorities or indicating slackness of duties are not reflected in the service record nor they have been brought on record by means of the counter affidavit,
consequently there cannot be any occasion for considering the said allegations as levelled in paragraph 9 of the counter affidavit.

20. As regards lodging of criminal case, a perusal of annexure 2 to the petition would indicate that the association had been formed by about 11 signatories of which only the petitioner has been singled out for compulsory retirement and thus the Court is of the view that lodging of the said criminal case cannot be considered to be a valid ground for compulsory retirement.

21. Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Gujarat vs Suryakant Chunilal Shah, 1999 (1) SCC 529 has held that while considering the case of employee for compulsory retirement public interest is of paramount importance.

entities.text: State of Gujarat vs Suryakant Chunilal Shah, 1999 (1) SCC 529
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Dishonest, corrupt and deadwood deserves to be dispensed with.
How efficient and honest an employee is, is to be assessed on the basis of materials on record which may also be ascertained from the confidential reports.
However there has to be tangible material against an employee warranting his compulsory retirement.

22. As already indicated above, no substantive material has been brought on record by the respondents to indicate that either the petitioner was not having a good general reputation or was a deadwood rather from the material which has been brought on record it emerges that the material which has been considered by the respondents while retiring the petitioner on compulsory grounds cannot be said to be sufficient or cogent for the purpose of passing an order of compulsory retirement as already indicated above.
23. Keeping in view the aforesaid discussion, the writ petition deserves to be allowed and is allowed.
A writ of certiorari is issued quashing the order dated 09.07.2019, a copy of which is annexure 1 to the writ petition.
A writ of mandamus is issued commanding the respondents to reinstate the petitioner in service with all consequential benefits including arrears of pay.
Let the respondents comply with this order within a period of 8 weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.

Order Date :- 16.4.2024 J. K. Dinkar  Ram Lal vs State Of U.P. Thru Prin.Secy. Home ... on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156284268/
